author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Temple Adath Yeshurun in Manchester is preparing for the High Holidays with a schedule that preserves core Jewish observances while adding more ways for families and newcomers to participate. Rosh Hashanah begins Friday evening, opening Hebrew year 5787, and the synagogue is making services available through free advance ticket registration and established security procedures.

Cantor Harriet Dunkerley, who became the congregation’s spiritual leader July 1, is introducing a family service Saturday afternoon before Tashlikh at Dorrs Pond. The program also includes visual versions of prayers intended to help participants follow the service. For Yom Kippur, the temple plans a family service September 21 at 1:30 p.m., along with study sessions and a cello-and-piano presentation of Kol Nidre.

The approach reflects the challenge facing many longstanding congregations: maintaining the structure and meaning of major observances while lowering practical barriers to participation. Temple Adath Yeshurun traces its history back more than a century and is New Hampshire’s oldest synagogue. Its 2026 schedule combines that institutional history with changes aimed at making the season understandable and welcoming across generations.
dek: Temple Adath Yeshurun is pairing longstanding observances with family services, visual prayer aids and open registration as the Hebrew year 5787 begins.
headline: Manchester synagogue blends tradition and access for High Holidays
